This report summarises a fit of the three-stage Bayesian selection
model for recorded Down-syndrome livebirth ascertainment in U.S. birth
certificate data (2016–2024). The model decomposes observed recording
into:

$$
P(R = 1 \mid X) = \theta_\text{LB}(\text{age}) \cdot \eta(X) \cdot s(X)
\;+\; (1 - \theta_\text{LB}\cdot \eta) \cdot f
$$

where $\theta_\text{LB}$ is the baseline DS livebirth rate in the
absence of selective termination (Morris 2002 / de Graaf 2015), $\eta = 1 -
\eta_\text{detect} \cdot \eta_\text{term}$ is the screening/termination
pass-through (Kuppermann / Natoli), $s$ is birth-certificate
sensitivity given a DS livebirth, and $f$
is a fixed false-positive probability per non-DS birth. See the
[selection guide](https://github.com/dspopulations/us-birth-certificates/blob/main/src/dspopulations_us_birth_certificates/selection/README.md)
for the implementation and current prior structure.

This decomposition is a prior-informed structural model. Birth
certificate counts alone do not separately identify baseline DS
livebirth prevalence, screening/termination, recording sensitivity, and
false positives. The Morris/de Graaf livebirth curve, the recording
surface, and the fixed false-positive rate constrain the split. The recording
surface reuses the recorded counts fitted by the likelihood, so it is not fully
independent evidence. Interpret the subcomponents conditional on these choices.

```{python}
run_config = read_json_artefact(Path("run_config.json"))
```

```{python}
Markdown(
```

## Cell aggregation

Births within the year range with known `down_ind`, `mage_c`, and the
required covariates are aggregated into cells keyed on year × age band
× race × education × payer × preterm × CCHD × NICU × assisted-
ventilation. A state/region column is not available in the project
DuckDB, so year effects on termination are modelled as a single
national trend term (`eta_term_year`) rather than a state-level
contrast.

```{python}
# | echo: false
cells = pd.read_parquet("cells.parquet")
n_total = int(cells["N_cell"].sum())
r_total = int(cells["R_cell"].sum())
pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "value": [
            len(cells),
            f"{n_total:,}",
            f"{r_total:,}",
            f"{r_total / max(n_total, 1):.3e}",
            f"{year_range[0]}–{year_range[1]}",
        ],
    },
    index=[
        "cells",
        "total livebirths (N)",
        "recorded DS (R)",
        "overall recorded rate",
        "year range",
    ],
)
```

## Convergence

```{python}
# | echo: false
summary_path = Path("summary.csv")
convergence_path = Path("convergence_summary.csv")
if summary_path.exists():
    summary = read_csv_artefact(summary_path, index_col=0)
    rhat_col = "r_hat" if "r_hat" in summary.columns else "rhat"
    max_rhat = summary[rhat_col].max() if rhat_col in summary.columns else float("nan")
    ess_cols = [c for c in ("ess_bulk", "ess_tail") if c in summary.columns]
    min_ess = summary[ess_cols].min().min() if ess_cols else float("nan")
    Markdown(
        f"- **max R̂**: {max_rhat:.4f} (target < 1.01)\n"
        f"- **min ESS**: {min_ess:.0f} (target ≥ 400)"
    )
elif convergence_path.exists():
    Markdown("*(see `convergence_summary.csv`)*")
else:
    Markdown("*(prior-only run, no posterior convergence summary available)*")
```

## Age curve, pinned Stage 1 anchor

Posterior baseline DS livebirth rate $\theta_\text{LB}$ per 1,000
livebirths, by maternal age band, against the Morris / de Graaf prior
means. The Morris prior is tightly pinned ($\sigma = 0.001$ on logit) so
posterior means should track the anchors closely, large deviations
indicate the age coding or cell aggregation has drifted. This is an
anchor-propagation check, not evidence that the birth-certificate data
estimated the biological age curve.

```{python}
# | echo: false
age_plot = Path("plots/age_curve.png")
if age_plot.exists():
    display(Image(str(age_plot)))
age_table = Path("tables/age_curve.csv")
if age_table.exists():
    display(read_csv_artefact(age_table).round(3))
```

## Correlation between termination and recording race effects

Per-race posterior scatter of the $\eta_\text{term}$ race effect
against the $s$ race effect. A high posterior correlation $|r| > 0.7$
is evidence of a remaining eta/s trade-off. A low correlation is not, by
itself, evidence that the data identified the split: under the current
anchored model, $s$ can be nearly fixed by the de Graaf prior surface,
so this diagnostic cannot show which source constrained the split. Small
variance alone does not determine correlation.

```{python}
# | echo: false
id_plot = Path("plots/identifiability.png")
if id_plot.exists():
    display(Image(str(id_plot)))
id_table = Path("tables/identifiability.csv")
if id_table.exists():
    id_df = read_csv_artefact(id_table)
    display(id_df.assign(correlation=id_df["correlation"].round(3),
                         abs_correlation=id_df["abs_correlation"].round(3)))
```

## Recording-anchor shrinkage

The primary check on the recording surface is the prior-to-posterior
readout for $s(\text{race}, \text{year})$. `sd_ratio` is posterior
standard deviation divided by prior standard deviation. `shift_in_prior_sd`
is the posterior mean's movement away from the prior mean, measured in
prior standard deviations. Values near `sd_ratio = 1` with little shift
mean the result is mostly anchor-carried; large shifts indicate tension
between the anchor and the fitted likelihood.

```{python}
# | echo: false
s_shrinkage_plot = Path("plots/s_anchor_shrinkage.png")
if s_shrinkage_plot.exists():
    display(Image(str(s_shrinkage_plot)))
s_shrinkage_table = Path("tables/s_anchor_shrinkage.csv")
if s_shrinkage_table.exists():
    shrink = read_csv_artefact(s_shrinkage_table)
    display(
        shrink[
            [
                "race",
                "year",
                "anchor_source",
                "sd_ratio",
                "shift_in_prior_sd",
                "interpretation",
            ]
        ].assign(
            sd_ratio=lambda d: d["sd_ratio"].round(2),
            shift_in_prior_sd=lambda d: d["shift_in_prior_sd"].round(2),
        )
    )
```

## Termination year trajectory

The plot shows the model's residual termination-stage year offsets.
Their interpretation depends on the other stage priors and recording surface.
The prior assigns the same standard deviation to each year's offset.

## Clinical and count-accounting limits

The model's clinical cells do not include clinical predictors in true prevalence.
Their true-case weights therefore do not supply a validated estimate of co-occurring
conditions among missed DS births. An external all-heart-defect prevalence also
does not match the narrower cyanotic-heart-disease checkbox.

The older race-decomposition output subtracts expected recorded flags from expected
true cases. With false-positive flags, that is not the expected number of missed
true cases, which is `sum(N * p_true * (1 - s))`. The old plot and subgroup shares
are omitted here until their accounting and clinical interpretation are corrected.

The [co-occurrence note](https://github.com/dspopulations/us-birth-certificates/blob/main/notes/20260622-predictors-bayesian-model.md)
describes a sensitivity formula that needs a supplied within-DS recording ratio.
It does not provide an independently validated population rate.

## Posterior predictive checks

Observed vs predicted recorded DS counts aggregated by stratum. The
posterior predictive bars should bracket the observed points (orange
markers); systematic misses in any stratum indicate missing structure.

```{python}
# | echo: false
for stratum in ("year_idx", "race_idx", "age_idx"):
    p = Path(f"plots/ppc_{stratum}.png")

        display(Image(str(p)))
```

## Expected true total

For each posterior parameter draw, the expected true total is
`sum(N_cell * p_ds_lb)`. Its interval describes uncertainty in that expectation
under the model. It does not add uncertainty in realised individual case status.

```{python}
# | echo: false
import numpy as np
import arviz as az
from dspopulations_us_birth_certificates.intervals import equal_tail_interval

idata = az.from_netcdf("idata.nc")
cells_full = pd.read_parquet("cells.parquet")
N = cells_full["N_cell"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
p_ds_lb = np.asarray(idata.posterior["p_ds_lb"].values)
true_counts_draws = (p_ds_lb * N[None, None, :]).sum(axis=-1)
total_true_lo, total_true_hi = equal_tail_interval(true_counts_draws)
pd.DataFrame({
    "quantity": ["Expected true DS livebirth total"],
    "mean": [float(true_counts_draws.mean())],
    "lo89": [float(total_true_lo)],
    "hi89": [float(total_true_hi)],
}).set_index("quantity")
```

## Classifier comparison and remaining limits

A classifier quota sets the number of selected unrecorded births. It does not
estimate the same target as the Bayesian expected true total. Do not compare
their counts or clinical shares as independent validations of missed cases.

Variant D fits a classifier-derived target with recording near one. That target
is not verified true status. The cell-count label `R` in a D run therefore has a
different meaning from observed recorded counts in the other variants.

The recording surface depends on surveillance extraction and extrapolation as
well as the recorded counts. Subgroup estimates and recent trends remain conditional
on it. No state identifier is available to check geographic recording effects.
The fixed false-positive probability is a working assumption with a different
denominator from a false-coded share among flags. Sampling profiles do not validate
these assumptions or guarantee convergence.
